title: अंश ६ · अध्याय ३

items.text:
सर्व्वेषामेव भूतानां त्रिविधः प्रितसञ्चरः ।
नैमित्तिकः प्राकृतिकस्तथैवात्यन्तिको मतः ॥ १ ॥
items.tr:
sarvveṣāmeva bhūtānāṃ trividhaḥ pritasañcaraḥ |
naimittikaḥ prākṛtikastathaivātyantiko mataḥ || 1 ||

items.text:
ब्राह्मो नैमित्तिकस्तेषां कल्पान्ते प्रतिसञ्चरः ।
आत्यन्तिकश्व मोक्षाख्यः प्राकृतो द्रिपरार्द्धिकः ॥ २ ॥
items.tr:
brāhmo naimittikasteṣāṃ kalpānte pratisañcaraḥ |
ātyantikaśva mokṣākhyaḥ prākṛto driparārddhikaḥ || 2 ||

items.speaker: मैत्रेय उवाच
items.text:
परार्द्धसंख्यां भगवन्! ममाचक्ष यया तु सः ।
द्रिगुणीकृतया ज्ञयेः प्राकृतः प्रतिसञ्चरः ॥ २ ॥
items.tr:
parārddhasaṃkhyāṃ bhagavan! mamācakṣa yayā tu saḥ |
driguṇīkṛtayā jñayeḥ prākṛtaḥ pratisañcaraḥ || 2 ||

items.speaker: पराशर उवाच
items.text:
स्थानात् स्थानं दशगुणमेकस्माद् गण्यते द्रिज!
ततोऽष्टादशमे स्थाने परार्द्धमभिघीयते ॥ ४ ॥
items.tr:
sthānāt sthānaṃ daśaguṇamekasmād gaṇyate drija!
tato'ṣṭādaśame sthāne parārddhamabhighīyate || 4 ||

items.text:
परार्द्धद्रिगुणं यत्तु प्राकृतः प्रलयो द्रिज!
तदाव्यक्तेऽखिलं व्यक्तं स्वहेतौ लयमेति वै ॥ ५ ॥
items.tr:
parārddhadriguṇaṃ yattu prākṛtaḥ pralayo drija!
tadāvyakte'khilaṃ vyaktaṃ svahetau layameti vai || 5 ||

items.text:
निमेषो मानुषो योऽयं मात्रामात्रप्रमाणतः ।
तैः पञ्चदशभिः काष्ठा त्रिंशत् काष्ठास्तथा कलाः ॥ ६ ॥
items.tr:
nimeṣo mānuṣo yo'yaṃ mātrāmātrapramāṇataḥ |
taiḥ pañcadaśabhiḥ kāṣṭhā triṃśat kāṣṭhāstathā kalāḥ || 6 ||

items.text:
नाड़िका तु प्रमाणेन कला दश च पञ्च च ।
उन्मानेनाम्भसः सा तु पलान्यर्द्धत्रयोदश ॥ ७ ॥
items.tr:
nāṛikā tu pramāṇena kalā daśa ca pañca ca |
unmānenāmbhasaḥ sā tu palānyarddhatrayodaśa || 7 ||

items.text:
हेममाषैः कृतिच्छिद्रश्वतुर्भिश्वतुरङ्गु लैः ।
मागधेन प्रमाणेन जलप्रस्थस्तु स स्मृतः ॥ ८ ॥
items.tr:
hemamāṣaiḥ kṛticchidraśvaturbhiśvaturaṅgu laiḥ |
māgadhena pramāṇena jalaprasthastu sa smṛtaḥ || 8 ||

items.text:
नाड़िकाभ्यामथ द्राभ्यां मुहूर्त्तो द्रिजसत्तम!
अहोरात्रं मुहूर्त्तास्तु त्रिंशन्मासो दिनैस्तथा ॥ ९ ॥
items.tr:
nāṛikābhyāmatha drābhyāṃ muhūrtto drijasattama!
ahorātraṃ muhūrttāstu triṃśanmāso dinaistathā || 9 ||

items.text:
मासैर्द्रादशभिर्वर्षमहोरात्रन्तु तद्दिवि ।
त्रिभिर्वर्षशतैर्वर्ष षष्ट्या चैवासुरद्रिषाम् ॥ १० ॥
items.tr:
māsairdrādaśabhirvarṣamahorātrantu taddivi |
tribhirvarṣaśatairvarṣa ṣaṣṭyā caivāsuradriṣām || 10 ||

items.text:
तैस्तु द्रादसोहस्त्र चतुर्युगमुदाह्टतम् ।
चतुर्युगसहस्त्रन्तु कथ्यते ब्रह्मणो दिनम् ॥ ११ ॥
items.tr:
taistu drādasohastra caturyugamudāhṭatam |
caturyugasahastrantu kathyate brahmaṇo dinam || 11 ||

items.text:
स कल्पोऽप्यत्र मनवश्वतुर्द्दश महामुने !
तदन्ते चैव मैत्रेय! ब्राह्मो नैमित्तिको लयः ॥ १२ ॥
items.tr:
sa kalpo'pyatra manavaśvaturddaśa mahāmune !
tadante caiva maitreya! brāhmo naimittiko layaḥ || 12 ||

items.text:
तंस्य स्वरूपमत्युग्र मैत्रेय गदतो मम ।
श्रृणुष्व प्राकृतं भूयस्तव वक्ष्याम्यहं लयम् ॥ १३ ॥
items.tr:
taṃsya svarūpamatyugra maitreya gadato mama |
śrṛṇuṣva prākṛtaṃ bhūyastava vakṣyāmyahaṃ layam || 13 ||

items.text:
चतुर्युगसहस्त्रान्ते क्षीणप्राये महीतले ।
अनावृष्टिरतीवोग्रा जायते शतवार्षिकी ॥ १४ ॥
items.tr:
caturyugasahastrānte kṣīṇaprāye mahītale |
anāvṛṣṭiratīvogrā jāyate śatavārṣikī || 14 ||

items.text:
ततो यान्यल्पसाराणि तानि तत्त्वान्यशेषतः ।
क्षयं यान्ति मुनिश्वेष्ठ!पार्थिवान्यत्र पीड़नात् ॥ १५ ॥
items.tr:
tato yānyalpasārāṇi tāni tattvānyaśeṣataḥ |
kṣayaṃ yānti muniśveṣṭha!pārthivānyatra pīṛanāt || 15 ||

items.text:
ततः स भगवान् विष्णू रुद्ररूपधरोऽव्ययः ।
क्षयाय यतते कर्त्तुमात्मस्थाः सकलाः वाजाः ॥ १६ ॥
items.tr:
tataḥ sa bhagavān viṣṇū rudrarūpadharo'vyayaḥ |
kṣayāya yatate karttumātmasthāḥ sakalāḥ vājāḥ || 16 ||

items.text:
ततः स भगवान् विष्णुर्भानोः सप्तसु रश्मिषु ।
स्थितः पिबत्यशेषाणि जलानि मुनिसत्तम ॥ १७ ॥
items.tr:
tataḥ sa bhagavān viṣṇurbhānoḥ saptasu raśmiṣu |
sthitaḥ pibatyaśeṣāṇi jalāni munisattama || 17 ||

items.text:
पीत्वार्म्भासि समस्तानि प्राणिभूमिगतानि वै ।
शोषं नयति मैत्रय!समस्तं पृथिवीतलम् ॥ १८ ॥
items.tr:
pītvārmbhāsi samastāni prāṇibhūmigatāni vai |
śoṣaṃ nayati maitraya!samastaṃ pṛthivītalam || 18 ||

items.text:
सरित्-समुद्र-शैलेषु शैल-प्रस्त्रवणेषु च ।
पातालेषु च यत्तोय तत् सर्व्वं नयति क्षयम् ॥ १९ ॥
items.tr:
sarit-samudra-śaileṣu śaila-prastravaṇeṣu ca |
pātāleṣu ca yattoya tat sarvvaṃ nayati kṣayam || 19 ||

items.text:
ततस्तस्यानुभावेन तोयाहारोपवृहिताः ।
त एव रश्मयः सप्त जायन्ते स्प्त भास्कराः ॥ २० ॥
items.tr:
tatastasyānubhāvena toyāhāropavṛhitāḥ |
ta eva raśmayaḥ sapta jāyante spta bhāskarāḥ || 20 ||

items.text:
अधश्वोदूर्ध्वञ्च ते दीप्यास्ततः स्पत दिंवाकराः ।
दहन्त्यशेषं त्रेलोक्यं सपातालतलं द्रिज ॥ २१ ॥
items.tr:
adhaśvodūrdhvañca te dīpyāstataḥ spata diṃvākarāḥ |
dahantyaśeṣaṃ trelokyaṃ sapātālatalaṃ drija || 21 ||

items.text:
दह्यमानन्तु तैर्दीप्तैस्त्रैलोक्यं द्रिज!भास्करेः ।
साद्रिनद्यर्णावाभोगं निःस्नेहमति जायते ॥ २२ ॥
items.tr:
dahyamānantu tairdīptaistrailokyaṃ drija!bhāskareḥ |
sādrinadyarṇāvābhogaṃ niḥsnehamati jāyate || 22 ||

items.text:
ततो निर्दग्धवृक्षाम्बु त्रैलोक्यमखिल द्रिज!
भवत्येका च वसुधा कूर्म्मपृष्ठोपमाकृतिः ॥ २३ ॥
items.tr:
tato nirdagdhavṛkṣāmbu trailokyamakhila drija!
bhavatyekā ca vasudhā kūrmmapṛṣṭhopamākṛtiḥ || 23 ||

items.text:
ततः कालाग्रिरुद्रोऽसौ भूत्वा सर्व्वहरो हरिः ।
शेषनिः श्वाससम्भूतः पातालानि बभिस्त्यधः ॥ २४ ॥
items.tr:
tataḥ kālāgrirudro'sau bhūtvā sarvvaharo hariḥ |
śeṣaniḥ śvāsasambhūtaḥ pātālāni babhistyadhaḥ || 24 ||

items.text:
पातालानि समस्तानि स दग्ध्वा ज्वलनो महान् ।
भूमिमभ्येत्य सकलं बभस्ति वसुधातलम् ॥ २५ ॥
items.tr:
pātālāni samastāni sa dagdhvā jvalano mahān |
bhūmimabhyetya sakalaṃ babhasti vasudhātalam || 25 ||

items.text:
भुवर्लोकं ततः सर्व्वं स्वर्लोकञ्च सुदारुणः ।
ज्वालामालामहावर्त्तस्तत्रैव परिवर्त्तते ॥ २६ ॥
items.tr:
bhuvarlokaṃ tataḥ sarvvaṃ svarlokañca sudāruṇaḥ |
jvālāmālāmahāvarttastatraiva parivarttate || 26 ||

items.text:
अम्बरीषमिवाभाति त्रैलोक्यमखिलं तदा ।
ज्वालावर्त्तपरीवारमुपक्षीणचराचरम् ॥ २७ ॥
items.tr:
ambarīṣamivābhāti trailokyamakhilaṃ tadā |
jvālāvarttaparīvāramupakṣīṇacarācaram || 27 ||

items.text:
ततस्तापपरीतास्तु लोकदूयनिवासिनः ।
कृताधिकारा गच्छन्ति महर्लोकं महामुने ॥ २८ ॥
items.tr:
tatastāpaparītāstu lokadūyanivāsinaḥ |
kṛtādhikārā gacchanti maharlokaṃ mahāmune || 28 ||

items.text:
तस्मादपि महातापतप्ता लोकास्ततः परम् ।
गच्छन्ति जनलोकं ते दशावृत्त्या परैषिणः ॥ २९ ॥
items.tr:
tasmādapi mahātāpataptā lokāstataḥ param |
gacchanti janalokaṃ te daśāvṛttyā paraiṣiṇaḥ || 29 ||

items.text:
ततो दग्ध्वा जगत् सर्व्वं रुद्ररूपी जनार्द्दनः।
मुखनिःश्वासजान् मेघान् करोति मुनिसत्तम् ॥ ३० ॥
items.tr:
tato dagdhvā jagat sarvvaṃ rudrarūpī janārddanaḥ|
mukhaniḥśvāsajān meghān karoti munisattam || 30 ||

items.text:
ततो गजकुलप्रख्यास्तड़ित्वन्तो निनादिनः ।
उत्तिष्ठन्ति तदा व्योम्रि घोराः संवर्त्तका घनाः ॥ ३१ ॥
items.tr:
tato gajakulaprakhyāstaṛitvanto ninādinaḥ |
uttiṣṭhanti tadā vyomri ghorāḥ saṃvarttakā ghanāḥ || 31 ||

items.text:
केचिन्नीलोतूपलश्यामाः केचित् कुमुदसन्निभाः ।
धूमवर्णा घनाः केचित् केचित् पीताः परोधराः ॥ ३२ ॥
items.tr:
kecinnīlotūpalaśyāmāḥ kecit kumudasannibhāḥ |
dhūmavarṇā ghanāḥ kecit kecit pītāḥ parodharāḥ || 32 ||

items.text:
केचिद्रासभवर्णाभा लाक्षारसनिभास्तथा ।
केचिद्रैदूर्य्यसङ्काशा इन्द्रनीलनिभाः परे ॥ ३३ ॥
items.tr:
kecidrāsabhavarṇābhā lākṣārasanibhāstathā |
kecidraidūryyasaṅkāśā indranīlanibhāḥ pare || 33 ||

items.text:
शङ्खकुन्दनिभाश्वान्ये जात्यञ्जननिबास्तथा ।
इन्द्रगोपनिभाः केचिनूमनः शिलनिभास्तथा ॥ ३४ ॥
items.tr:
śaṅkhakundanibhāśvānye jātyañjananibāstathā |
indragopanibhāḥ kecinūmanaḥ śilanibhāstathā || 34 ||

items.text:
चाषपत्रनिभाः केचिदुत्तिष्ठन्ति घना घनाः ।
केचित् पुरवरावकाराः केचित् पर्व्वतसन्नभाः ॥ ३५ ॥
items.tr:
cāṣapatranibhāḥ keciduttiṣṭhanti ghanā ghanāḥ |
kecit puravarāvakārāḥ kecit parvvatasannabhāḥ || 35 ||

items.text:
कूटागारनिभाश्वान्ये केचित् स्थूलनिभा घनाः ।
महारावा महाकायाः पूरयन्ति नभस्तलम् ॥ ३६ ॥
items.tr:
kūṭāgāranibhāśvānye kecit sthūlanibhā ghanāḥ |
mahārāvā mahākāyāḥ pūrayanti nabhastalam || 36 ||

items.text:
वर्षन्तस्ते महासारै-स्तमग्रिमतिभैरवम् ।
शमयन्त्यखिलं विप्र! त्रैलोक्यान्तरविस्तृतम् ॥ ३७ ॥
items.tr:
varṣantaste mahāsārai-stamagrimatibhairavam |
śamayantyakhilaṃ vipra! trailokyāntaravistṛtam || 37 ||

items.text:
नष्टे चाग्रौ शतं तेऽपि वर्षाणामनिवारिताः ।
प्लावयन्तो जगत् सर्वं वर्षन्ति मुनिसत्तम ॥ ३८ ॥
items.tr:
naṣṭe cāgrau śataṃ te'pi varṣāṇāmanivāritāḥ |
plāvayanto jagat sarvaṃ varṣanti munisattama || 38 ||

items.text:
धाराभिरक्षमात्राभिः प्लावयित्वाखिलं भुवम् ।
भुवर्लोकं तथैवोर्द्ध्व प्लावयन्ति दिवं द्रिज ॥ ३९ ॥
items.tr:
dhārābhirakṣamātrābhiḥ plāvayitvākhilaṃ bhuvam |
bhuvarlokaṃ tathaivorddhva plāvayanti divaṃ drija || 39 ||

items.text:
अन्धरारीकृते लोके नष्टे स्थावरजङ्गमे ।
वर्षन्ति ते महामेघा वर्षाणामधिकं शतम ॥ ४० ॥
items.tr:
andharārīkṛte loke naṣṭe sthāvarajaṅgame |
varṣanti te mahāmeghā varṣāṇāmadhikaṃ śatama || 40 ||

en_chapter: Parāçara said The dissolution of existing beings is of three kinds, incidental, elemental and absolute. The incidental is that which relates to Brahmā and takes place at the end of a Kalpa: the elemental is that which occurs after two Parārdhas; the absolute is final liberation from existence.
Maitreya said:—"Tell me, O excellent preceptor, what is the enumeration of a Parārdha, the expiration of two of which is the period of elemental dissolution".

Parāçara said:—Parardha, O Maitreya, is that number which takes place in the eighteenth place of figures enumerated according to the rule of decimal notation. At the end of twice that period elemental dissolution takes place when all the discrete products of nature are withdrawn into Their indiscrete source. The shortest period of time is Mātrā which is equal to the twinkling of the human eye; fifteen Mātrā make a Kāshthā; thirty Kāshthās one Kalā: fifteen Kalās one Nādhikā. A Nādhikā is determined by a measure of water with a vessel made of twelve Palas and a half of copper in the bottom of which there is to be a hole made with a tube of gold of the weight of four Māshas and four inches long. According to the Māgadha measure the vessel should hold a Prastha (or sixteen Palas) of water. Two of these Nādis make one Muhurta; thirty of which make one day and night. Thirty such periods constitute a month; twelve months make a year, or a day and night of the celestials; and three hundred and sixty such days, constitute a year of the celestials. An aggregate of four ages consists of twelve thousand divine years; and a thousand periods of four ages complete a day of Brahmā. That period is also termed a Kalpa during which fourteen Munis preside and at the end of it takes place the incidental or Brahmā dissolution. The nature of this dissolution is very dreadful; hear, I shall describe this as well as that which takes place as the elemental dissolution.

At the end of a thousand period of four ages the earth is for the most part exhausted. A total dearth takes place which lasts for a hundred years; and on account of the failure of food all beings become languid and exanimate and at last entirely die. The eternal Vishnu then takes the character of Rudra the destroyer and comes down to reunite all his creatures with himself. He enters into the seven rays of the sun, drinks up all the waters of the earth and causes all moisture, whatever in living bodies or in the soil to evaporate, thus drying up the whole earth. Thus fed with his intervention with profuse moisture, the seven solar rays dilate to seven suns, whose radiance glows above, below and on every side and sets the three worlds and Pātāla on fire. The three worlds, consumed by these suns, become rugged and deformed all over their mountains, rivers and seas; and the earth bare of verdure, and destitute of moisture alone remains resembling in appearance the back of a tortoise. Hari, the destroyer of all things, in the form of Rudra, who is the flame of time, becomes the scorching breath of the serpent Sesha and thereby reduces Pātāla to ashes. The great fire, when it has reduced all the divisions of Pātāla to ashes, proceeds to the earth and consumes it also. A vast whirlpool of eddying flame then spreads to the region of the atmosphere and the sphere of the celestials and wraps them in ruin. The three spheres shew like a frying pan amidst the surrounding flames that prey upon all movable and stationary things. O great saint, the inhabitants of the two upper spheres, having satisfied their respective duties and being assailed by the heat, repair to Maharloka. When that becomes heated its inhabitants, who after the full period of stay, are desirous of ascending to higher regions depart for the Janaloka.

Having consumed the whole universe in the person of Rudra, Janārddana, breathes fourth heavy clouds, and those called Samvartta resembling huge elephants in bulk overspread the sky, roaring and darting lightnings. Some are as white as the water-lily, some are dusky like smoke; some are yellow; some are of a dun colour, like that of an ass; some like ashes sprinkled on the forehead; some are deep blue, as the lapis lazuly; some azure like the sapphire; some are white at the couch or the jasmine; some are black as colly rum; some are like the lady-bird; some are of fierceness of red arsenic and some are like the wing of the painted joy. Such is the colour of these massy clouds; in form some resemble towns, some mountains, some are like houses and hovels and some are like columns. Huge in size and loud in thunder they fill space. Showering down torrents of water, those clouds quench the dreadful fires which involve the three worlds and then rain incessantly a hundred years and deluge the whole universe. Showering down in drops as large as dice these rains overspread the earth and fill the middle region and inundate the celestial sphere. The world is now enshrouded in darkness and all things animate and inanimate having perished, the clouds continue to pour down waters for more than a hundred years.
